name: nvc
why: An open-source VHDL compiler and simulator, a rare chance to simulate hardware circuits from the terminal.

brief.what_it_is: NVC is a free, open-source VHDL compiler and simulator that implements almost all of VHDL-2008 (IEEE 1076-2008). You give it VHDL source files and a top-level testbench entity name, and it analyses, elaborates and runs the simulation from the terminal. It uses LLVM to compile the design to native machine code. It is a simulator only and does not synthesize anything for an FPGA or ASIC. Waveforms can be viewed in GTKWave or Surfer.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it simply as a free software VHDL compiler and simulator. The README stresses simulation performance as a particular emphasis, and says it has been used to simulate several real-world designs.
brief.how_it_works: Simulation runs in three steps, which the README compares to compiling, linking and executing a software program: analysing the source files (-a), elaborating the design (-e), and running the simulation (-r). Because NVC uses LLVM to compile VHDL to native code, the simulated design runs as machine code. Vendor and verification libraries such as OSVVM, UVVM, Vivado and Quartus are installed with nvc --install <name>, into ~/.nvc/lib.

commands_seen.context: Elaborate the design with my_tb as the top-level testbench entity.
Analyse, elaborate and run in a single command.
Read the full manual after installation.
Install the Windows installer via winget.
Generate the configure script when building from a Git clone.
Configure a separate build directory (in-tree builds are not supported).
Compile the OSVVM verification framework libraries. Similar commands exist for uvvm, ise, vivado, quartus, icecube2 and fmf.

brief.install_notes: On macOS, brew install nvc is the easy route. It is also packaged for FreeBSD, Gentoo, Arch (AUR) and several other distributions, and there is a Windows installer and winget package. Building from source needs autoconf, automake, flex, check and LLVM (minimum 8.0; 8 through 21 tested), plus zlib, libdw, libffi and libzstd development packages. The README gives apt and dnf package lists. Build out-of-tree with mkdir build && cd build, then ../configure, make and sudo make install. Windows is supported only under MSYS2 with the Clang x64 environment, using a pacman package list. Vendor and framework libraries are installed afterwards with nvc --install. Docker image ghcr.io/nickg/nvc and a setup-nvc GitHub Action exist for CI.
brief.standout: It is a rare open-source VHDL simulator with a performance focus, using LLVM to JIT-compile designs to native code. Its README also documents support for common verification frameworks (OSVVM, UVVM, VUnit, cocotb) and for FPGA vendor simulation libraries, which is unusual for a free tool.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage says the most recent version is 1.23.0, released 19th September 2026, with release notes linked. The README has a build-status badge, a coverage badge, and a note that the master branch is intended to be stable for day-to-day use. I did not see a last-commit date, so I cannot confirm recent commit activity beyond that.
brief.caveats: It is not a synthesizer. It does not support PSL. Experimental Verilog and VHDL-2019 support is under development. The VITAL libraries have unclear licence status, and the README says distributors with strict free-software rules should strip them or configure with --disable-vital. The README says the project is a spare-time hobby with limited time for patch review, and it comes with no warranty and no expected support. Windows support is limited to MSYS2. Building from source has real dependency requirements.
quotes: NVC is not a synthesizer.  That is, it does not output something that could be used to program an FPGA or ASIC.
NVC has a particular emphasis on simulation performance and uses LLVM to compile VHDL to native machine code.
Please remember that this software is provided to you with NO WARRANTY and no expectation of support, but I will do my best to help with any issues you encounter.
